attribution.note: Zitron states all three assertions in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the three present-tense assertions, including the restriction to non-technical users for software delivery.

contract.note: The supplied standard for compelling evidence is an ordinary, fair reading of the unqualified denial. Credible measured gains need not establish economy-wide improvement. The contract appropriately separates the three assertions.

evidence.note: The pre-post randomized experiment finds faster professional writing with improved quality. It contradicts the denial of compelling productivity evidence, while establishing neither worker replacement nor software-delivery gains.

The published workplace study supplies comparison-based evidence of higher output per hour before the statement. Its single-firm scope and heterogeneous effects limit generalization but do not negate the measured gains.

This timely company disclosure links headcount reductions to AI and broader efficiency efforts. It does not isolate actual AI-caused position replacement or independently verify management's attribution.
The randomized slowdown result limits generalization across work settings. It does not negate positive studies or test software delivery by non-technical users.

The pre-post follow-up qualifies the earlier slowdown finding. Selection effects and uncertain estimates prevent a firm productivity conclusion; the participants also do not match the non-technical population.

reviews.rationale: The productivity-evidence assertion is contradicted by credible studies publicly available before June 15, 2026. METR's slowdown demonstrates variation without erasing those findings. Worker replacement and non-technical users' software-delivery effects remain unresolved; neither is established as false or supported by this packet.
